executive_summary: Chapter 7 establishes that matter consists of sub-microscopic constituent particles held by interparticle forces. It explains solid, liquid, and gas properties via interparticle spacing and attraction, thermal kinetic energy driving motion, and phase changes (melting, boiling).
key_takeaways: Master core concepts of Particulate Nature of Matter.
Understand real-world applications and experimental activities.
Analyze cause-and-effect relations and scientific definitions.

essential_vocabulary.definition: The void distance existing between constituent particles of a substance.
Attractive binding force holding constituent particles together.
